decisions.reason: It extends the firm's core second-channel security offer, and in a growing market with in-house R&D and likely slack there is little reason to drop a newly launched product absent signs of shortfall.

A mobile PDF signature function is close to the established authentication and signing business, so its fit with existing capabilities and the firm's strategic direction makes retention more likely than problemistic search.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture builds directly on the firm's cryptography and platform strengths, and without negative performance evidence management would likely continue to support it.

This message-delivery robot fits the secure communication portfolio but is somewhat more niche, so it faces more review risk, though the firm's breadth and organisational slack still make keeping it more likely.

The hardware signature token is related to the core offer but is a more specific and potentially costlier hardware add-on, so it has a higher drop risk even though the firm is still likely to retain it while results remain uncertain.
A payment-network compliance suite matches the firm's regulatory-security positioning and should benefit from existing expertise, making continuation more likely than withdrawal in the near term.
